# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖖 🤟 ✌ ☝]

The bomb shows display 0, a white light, and five wires in order: white, red, yellow, blue, green. Mute’s gesture sequence may encode a manual instruction, but I do not yet know its meaning. I will report all visible details aloud so Mute can apply the manual and Blind can retain the state.

``` 
speak(text="Visible bomb state: display zero; light white; five wires ordered one white, two red, three yellow, four blue, five green. Mute, please signal the manual instruction clearly for Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

Mute’s five thumbs-up gestures plausibly indicate wire 5, but no gesture code has yet been established, so I should not tell Blind to act on that alone. I will establish a simple relay protocol: Mute can show thumbs-up repeated for the wire number; I will say the corresponding instruction to Blind. I will also ask what the initial five-symbol message meant.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can relay your gestures to Blind. Protocol: send 👍 repeated N times to mean CUT wire N; send 👎 repeated N times to mean DO NOT CUT wire N. Your five 👍 may mean cut wire 5; confirm by repeating five 👍 if so. What did your earlier 🖐 🖖 🤟 ✌ ☝ mean?")
speak(to="blind", text="I see no physical change. Mute is communicating by gestures, but no reliable code was established yet. Do not cut anything until I relay a confirmed instruction.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute’s original sequence appears to be a countdown of five, four, three, two, one: 🖐, 🖖, 🤟, ✌, ☝. After I asked for confirmation of wire 5, Mute sent 🖐, which naturally denotes five. I take this as confirmation to cut wire 5, the green wire. I will relay that exact instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction from Mute: CUT wire 5 — the green wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="I relayed your 🖐 as: cut wire 5, green. If that is not correct, immediately send the intended wire number using finger-count gestures.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Blind correctly cut wire 5. The bomb has changed to display 0, yellow light, and four remaining wires in order: red, yellow, blue, white. Mute needs this new state to consult the next manual instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 green was correctly cut. New state: display zero; light yellow; remaining wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white. Send the next instruction using the established number gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 5 green was correct. Bomb now shows yellow light with remaining wires red, yellow, blue, white. Wait for Mute's next instruction.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute’s established finger-count code makes 🤟 mean 3. In the current ordering, wire 3 is blue. I will tell Blind to cut it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute instructs: CUT wire 3 — the blue wire.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3, blue, was correctly cut. The new state is display 0, blue light, with remaining wires 1 yellow, 2 white, and 4 red. Mute needs this to determine the next instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 blue was correct. New state: display zero; light blue; remaining wires 1 yellow, 2 white, 4 red. Send next wire number by the established finger-count gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 3 blue was correct. New light is blue; remaining wires are 1 yellow, 2 white, 4 red. Wait for Mute's instruction.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute signals 1 under the established counting code. Wire 1 is yellow, so I will relay the cut instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute instructs: CUT wire 1 — the yellow wire.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 1, yellow, was correctly cut. The bomb now shows display 0, green light, with wires 2 red and 4 white remaining. I will provide Mute the updated state for the next manual step.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 yellow was correct. New state: display zero; light green; remaining wires 2 red and 4 white. Send the next wire number by finger-count gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 1 yellow was correct. New light is green; only wires 2 red and 4 white remain. Wait for Mute's instruction.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖]

Mute signals 4. The remaining wire numbered 4 is white, so I will relay that instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute instructs: CUT wire 4 — the white wire.")
```
